skill.name: cavecrew
skill.description: Decision guide for choosing cavecrew subagents that locate code, make small edits, and review diffs with compressed output.

content.value_statement: Long coding sessions lose context when subagents return verbose results. Cavecrew guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code toward compact investigator, builder, and reviewer agents.
actual_capabilities: Guides when to use cavecrew-investigator to locate definitions, callers, or usages.
Guides when to use cavecrew-builder for clear edits in one or two files.
Guides when to use cavecrew-reviewer for concise diff or file reviews.
Compares cavecrew agents with vanilla Explore and Code Reviewer options.
Defines output contracts and chaining patterns for locate, fix, and verify workflows.
limitations: It is a decision guide, not an executable tool by itself.
It depends on the referenced cavecrew subagents being installed and available.
It favors compressed output, so details and rationale may be sparse.
It is not suited to broad features, large refactors, or architecture discussions.

use_cases.title: Find Code References Quickly
use_cases.description: Use the investigator agent when a developer needs concise file and line references before editing.

use_cases.title: Apply Small Focused Fixes
use_cases.description: Use the builder agent when the scope is obvious and limited to one or two files.

use_cases.title: Review a Diff Efficiently
use_cases.description: Use the reviewer agent when a team wants compact bug findings without extended commentary.

prompt_templates.title: Choose the Right Cavecrew Agent
prompt_templates.prompt: Use cavecrew to decide whether this task needs investigator, builder, reviewer, or the main thread: [describe task].

prompt_templates.title: Locate Code Before Editing
prompt_templates.prompt: Use cavecrew-investigator to find where [symbol or behavior] is defined and where it is used. Return compact file and line references.

prompt_templates.title: Make a Small Verified Edit
prompt_templates.prompt: Use cavecrew-builder for this focused change in [file or files]: [specific change]. Keep the edit limited and verify the result.

prompt_templates.title: Chain Locate Fix Review
prompt_templates.prompt: Use cavecrew to locate the issue, apply a one or two file fix if the scope is clear, then review the diff for regressions.

output_examples.input: Find every caller of the account validation routine.
output_examples.output: A compact list of matching files, line numbers, symbols, and short notes suitable for the main thread.

output_examples.input: Fix this obvious typo in the payment settings label.
output_examples.output: A short edit summary with the changed file, affected lines, and a verification result.

output_examples.input: Review the current diff for bugs only.
output_examples.output: A concise findings list sorted by file and line, or a clear statement that no issues were found.

best_practices: Use investigator before builder when the target file is not already known.
Keep builder requests limited to one or two clear files.
Use vanilla review agents when you need rationale, alternatives, or architecture advice.
anti_patterns: Do not use builder for broad features or cross-cutting refactors.
Do not ask reviewer for general feedback when you need design commentary.
Do not use cavecrew when a direct one-line answer is already enough.

faq.question: What does this skill do?
faq.answer: It guides when to delegate coding work to cavecrew investigator, builder, or reviewer agents.

faq.question: Does it run commands or edit files directly?
faq.answer: No. The skill is documentation that tells the assistant which subagent pattern to use.

faq.question: Which tools can use it?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: When should I use cavecrew-investigator?
faq.answer: Use it when you need compact file and line references for definitions, callers, or usages.

faq.question: When should I avoid cavecrew-builder?
faq.answer: Avoid it for unclear scope, more than two files, large features, or broad refactors.

faq.question: Why is the output terse?
faq.answer: The skill prioritizes compressed subagent output to preserve the main conversation context.
